product.name: Atlas Evidence Review
product.summary: A local-first review workspace for a bounded release evidence packet.
product.problem: Reviewers need a traceable experience for examining evidence without confusing provider completion with Product readiness.
product.affectedUsers: Product owners, designers, release engineers, and accountable reviewers
product.desiredOutcome: Demonstrate one exact candidate-only Product-to-Figma-to-Product design loop with independently verifiable boundaries.
successSignals: Every loop stage is bound to an exact deterministic receipt
Missing permission, stale target, and return conflict states fail closed
No external write, import, approval, baseline, readiness, or implementation effect is claimed
product.firstWorkflow: Inspect a release evidence packet and its bounded design-review state.

initiative.title: Review the Atlas evidence experience
initiative.outcome: A deterministic local artifact exposes the full governed design loop and its unresolved authority boundaries.
scope: Candidate design package and outbound preview
Candidate return, comparison, review, approval, baseline, drift, and impact evidence
Product Studio and four-host read-only projection binding

failureCases.trigger: The deterministic write-review candidate has no granted permission evidence.
failureCases.recovery: An accountable human may provide current bounded permission evidence and request a new preview.

failureCases.trigger: The exact target version differs from the version bound to the outbound preview.
failureCases.recovery: Re-read the bounded target, recompute the delta, and require a new human confirmation.

failureCases.trigger: The local returned-snapshot fixture conflicts with the exact outbound design-package candidate.
failureCases.recovery: Route the exact conflict set to accountable human resolution before any approval or baseline candidate is reconsidered.

limitations: This is a deterministic local fixture, not real Product research, returned current Figma content, or a production dataset.
No Figma or provider connection, authentication, permission grant, request, transfer, write, import, usage, cost, or semantic-quality assessment occurs.
Recorded human-review, approval, and baseline objects remain candidates; accountable authority, enforced separation of duties, effective approval, and an actual Baseline Set are not established.
Native host and Product Owner acceptance, readiness, security completion, release authorization, and deployment approval remain absent.
